title: Contract-backed throughput shims and anticipatory autoscaler for Dedicated pools
creator: Anika Patel
description: Background: Large tenants on Dedicated pools require stable throughput guarantees (tokens/sec) while retaining predictable tail latency. Current autoscaler reacts to sustained GPU utilization and queue depth but often overshoots or lags for bursty enterprise traffic, causing either wasted reserved capacity or user-visible degradation. Goal: implement a "contract-backed throughput shim" layer that enforces per-tenant throughput contracts at the routing edge, emits autoscaler hints based on short-term consumption forecasts, and provides a soft-drop policy that preserves SLOs for priority lanes.
success_criteria: 1) Tenants with committed throughput see >=95% of contracted throughput during normal operating windows without significant tail-latency regressions. 2) Autoscaler hints reduce scale-up latency by >=30% measured from hint emission to additional GPU readiness in controlled experiments. 3) End-to-end failure mode: under severe overload, P0 lanes maintain 99.9th percentile latency within 2x baseline while lower-priority lanes are shed gracefully.
design_summary: - Contract shim: lightweight admission proxy at the ingress that tracks per-tenant token consumption vs contract in sliding windows. Implements exact-rate contracts (hard minimum reservation) and opportunistic burst credits. - Anticipatory autoscaler: short-horizon forecast (30s-3min) using EWMA + recent burst detection to emit scale-up hints to the fleet autoscaler. Hints include desired extra GPU count and urgency score. - Soft-drop policy: when contracts can't be satisfied, the shim applies progressive degradation: 1) deferable batching + extended queueing up to a capped depth, 2) probabilistic de-prioritization for best-effort lanes, 3) targeted soft-drop with adaptive drop probability tied to urgency and contract deficit. - Observability: new metrics (contract_use_ratio, hint_latency, soft_drop_rate) surfaced to Console with per-tenant breakdowns and suggested remediation actions.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - We chose short-horizon heuristics (EWMA + burst detector) over heavy ML forecasting to keep runtime predictable and avoid cold-start model latency. - Exact-rate enforcement at ingress trades off some latency for deterministic throughput guarantees; we will allow an "opt-out" flag for latency-sensitive, non-committed tenants. - Autoscaler hints are advisory and never force immediate provisioning; final scale decisions remain in autoscaler to respect multi-tenant consolidation policies.
api_changes: - Ingress config: add `throughput_contracts` block (tenant_id, tokens_per_sec, burst_capacity, priority_lane). - Shim telemetry API: `/v1/ingress/metrics/contract/{tenant}` for real-time contract stats. - Autoscaler hook: `/internal/hints/scale` accepts (pool_id, suggested_gpus, urgency_score, expiry).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): prototype admission shim in canary cluster, basic contract enforcement and metrics emission. Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement anticipatory hinter, integrate with autoscaler read path; add soft-drop strategies. Phase 3 (2 weeks): observability + runbook + canary rollout to 2 low-traffic Dedicated pools. Phase 4 (follow-up): opt-in customer trials, iterate on heuristics and cost-model adjustments.
risks: - Incorrect hinting could cause unnecessary cold starts and cost overruns. Mitigation: caps on suggested_gpus and low initial urgency multiplier. - Overly aggressive soft-drop may harm retention for lower-tier customers. Mitigation: conservative default drop curves and telemetry to track business metrics. - Complexity of per-tenant state could increase memory pressure on ingress proxies; mitigation: bounded state windows and TTL eviction.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal QA + integration tests (unit, perf, chaos). 2) Canary shard with synthetic tenants and replayed traffic. 3) Gradual expansion to customer-facing Dedicated pools with opt-in toggle. 4) Post-rollout A/B evaluation comparing contract fulfillment and autoscale cost delta.
testing_plan: - Microbenchmarks: admission latency added by shim (target <= 0.8ms tail). - Stress tests: synthetic burst patterns to validate soft-drop behavior and contract preservation. - Autoscaler integration tests: measure time from hint to additional capacity readiness under cloud warm pools. - Regression: ensure non-committed tenants do not see increased 95th percentile latencies.
observability_and_alerting: Metrics: contract_use_ratio, contract_breach_count, short_forecast_variance, hint_emission_rate, hint_ack_latency, soft_drop_rate. Alerts: contract_breach_count > 5m threshold, hint_ack_latency > 30s in >10% of events, soft_drop_rate sudden rise. Dashboards: per-pool and per-tenant contract health with suggested tuning actions.
open_questions: 1) What default enforcement window sizes should we pick (30s/60s/120s)? 2) Should we allow cross-tenant credit transfers inside the same org? 3) How to surface cost-impact forecasts to sales/finance for committed customers?
